title: Accelerate: The State of DevOps with Dr. Nicole Forsgren
summary: Forsgren on the 2018 Accelerate State of DevOps report: speed and stability move together, industry does not matter, small changes have a small blast radius.

assertions.quote: speed and stability move in tandem the highest performers get both there is no tradeoff

verdicts.note: Five years of DORA survey clustering show throughput and stability correlate, but the data are self-reported and correlational rather than experimental.

Six years of survey data show speed and stability are outcomes that enable each other: cluster analysis finds elite performers do significantly better on all four metrics and low performers worse on all, rather than trading throughput for stability.

assertions.quote: there was no statistical evidence that it matters

verdicts.note: The DORA models found no industry effect, but a null result from a voluntary survey sample does not prove the practices work equally everywhere.

Controlling for industry, DORA found no evidence that industry affects SDO performance except retail (which did slightly better), including highly regulated financial services and government; organisation size over 5,000 employees did predict lower performance.

assertions.quote: when you do introduce code you're introducing very very small pieces of code so that introduction is small it has a small blast radius
the big difference there is we usually skip testing which is the time that we should not be skipping testing

verdicts.note: Skipped testing in emergency changes is widely reported in incident reviews but not quantified here.

assertions.quote: they have incredibly efficient test Suites they have great parallelization so that they can be very very strategic about exploratory testing

verdicts.note: DORA reports less manual testing among elite performers, but this is a self-reported association rather than a measured cause.

Elite performers report automated unit tests 87% vs 57% for low performers, acceptance tests 58% vs 28%, and automated production deployment 69% vs 17%; the report does not ask about exploratory or manual testing.

assertions.quote: when developers help write tests we write better and more testable code
if it takes you months to get a change through what happens to your security posture when you need to get a patch through

verdicts.note: Patch latency follows directly from lead time; the risk exposure is real though its magnitude varies.

The report argues high SDO performance lets organisations keep up with compliance and regulatory changes and deliver security patches quickly and reliably; this is reasoning from the delivery metrics, not a measured patch-latency result.
